newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek fuel to keep up market rally.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek fuel to keep up market rally.

text.p: German shares again surged to a new record high on Tuesday but failed to sustain the gains to end the bourse session slightly higher, traders said.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 4.77 points at 3,067.06 points but below a new record at 3,083.07 points.
Dealers said a weaker German debt market, hurt by a 1.1 percent rise in German industrial orders in 1996, and bouts of profit-taking weighed on the market.
But dollar-sensitive stocks, including industrial group Daimler-Benz AG and electronics group Siemens AG, helped to keep the index relatively buoyant.

Dealings in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings were expected to remain relatively steady as the market remained positive ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve committee meeting at which the U.S. central bank was expected to keep rates steady.
The market was also expected to find some underpinning from the dollar, which remained above the key level of 1.64 marks seen as important for the German market's continuing advance.

But traders were still split between the perception that the share market, already trading around record levels, was due for a correction against hopes for an German economic upturn that would feed into corporate earnings.
"Fundamentally, there are still lots of things to be bullish about, but a correction of some kind has been overdue for some time now," one dealer said.

Market attention focused on telecom issues as Veba AG would not comment on reports it had been approached by SBC Communications but confirmed that it was talking to several potential buyers of a stake in its telecoms venture.
Veba could have a stake of up to 22 percent available in Veba's telecoms venture with RWE should the third partner, Britain's Cable and Wireless, opts to pull out of the alliance as widely expected.

The German government on Tuesday also awarded a consortium owned by British Telecom Plc and utility Viag AG the country's fourth mobile telephone licence, propelling Viag's shares up 18.50 marks to 702.50 marks.

Among other shares, software group SAP AG fell three percent, or down 7.30 marks to 243.20 marks, after a bank consortium announced plans to offer shares held by a trust and once owned by a SAP co-founder who has since left the group.
Metallgesellschaft AG fell 75 pfennigs to 33.05 marks after some traders said the industrial and engineering group's meeting with analysts was not received favourably.
